'''Game Players Network''' (GPN) was a volunteer community site that, in the years around Decipher's loss of the ''Star Wars'' license, hosted Star Wars CCG decklists, tournament reports, strategy, interviews, and official [[Players Committee]] announcements. Decipher pointed remaining SWCCG support at GPN's news pages and PC forum after 31 December 2001.<ref name="decipher2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030111000000id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Star Wars CCG], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 January 2003)</ref>

The domain is gone; the Star Wars section survives in Wayback captures such as [https://web.archive.org/web/20041009222615/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/games.asp?gm=starwars games.asp?gm=starwars] (9 October 2004).<ref name="gpnhome">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041009222615/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/games.asp?gm=starwars Star Wars home], gameplayersnetwork.com (Wayback, 9 October 2004)</ref>

== What it was ==

Scott Gaeta described GPN as a place for "the most useful and up to date information" on favorite games, with volunteers contributing articles, reviews, and interviews. Members were asked to post decks, join discussion, and leave constructive reviews. The About page listed Gaeta as editor and publisher, Tim McKnight as card-game editor, and separate editors for RPG, miniatures, and board games.<ref name="about">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041011081657/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/about/default.asp About GPN], gameplayersnetwork.com (Wayback, 11 October 2004)</ref>

The Star Wars section sat under Card Games. Its left rail was:

* '''Decks''' — Standard, Theme/Fun, Scenario
* '''Tournament Reports'''
* '''Strategy Articles'''
* '''Discussion''' (forums)
* '''Features Archives'''
* '''News Archives'''

A member center, club/group locator, and a two-rule house policy (no bad language; no flaming) sat on every page.<ref name="gpnhome" />

== Official PC channel ==

Decipher stopped publishing Star Wars CCG, Young Jedi, and Jedi Knights. Its Star Wars home page then said tournament, rules, and gameplay support came from the volunteer Players Committee "through Game Players Network's news pages and the Player's Committee forum."<ref name="decipher2002" />

Warren Holland's 25 January 2002 Players' Committee letter noted GPN assistance with communications and prize shipping after 30 April 2002.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002)</ref> The same day Gaeta posted on GPN that Holland had named the six core Advocates. GPN's offer to support the committee had been accepted.<ref name="news">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041012153722/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/news.asp?gm=starwars News Archives], gameplayersnetwork.com (Wayback, 12 October 2004)</ref>

GPN's ''rulesupdate.pdf'' later printed the former PC oval logo, shown as the "GPN era" mark on [[History of the Players Committee]].<ref name="gpnlogo">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060212114753/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/starwars/rulesupdate.pdf rulesupdate.pdf], gameplayersnetwork.com (Wayback, 12 February 2006)</ref>

McKnight's GAMA report was the public hint of [[WARS TCG]]: Decipher was "bringing back the Star Wars CCG mechanic" in a game that fall, without naming a license.<ref name="news" />

On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), [[Scott Gaeta]] said GPN had about 40 to 50 volunteers (writers, news staff and programmers). It had answered Decipher's call for Players Committee volunteers, aiming to become "the home of the Players Committee". GPN offered the committee web space, coverage and support for its tournament formats, and a separate message board for player suggestions. It also offered the web programming for posting virtual-card game text on decipher.com.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=678s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 11:18. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref>

Other Features pieces on the same archive are player-facing rather than PC-official: Duane Bruun's language primer ("TLOSWCCG"), a Justin Pakes interview on Theed Palace, and Michael Raveling on deployment.<ref name="features" />

== Decklists ==

The deck desk was a rated, user-submitted catalog. The October 2004 home page listed a rolling "Top Decks in the Last 30 Days." The catalog ran to sixty-plus listing pages from late 2001 through 2005, with titles already using the era's slang (WYS, QMC, MKOS, TDIGWATT, Hidden Base, ISB Operations).<ref name="decks2005">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050327114018/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/decks.asp?gm=starwars&ord=&pg=1 Star Wars Decks], gameplayersnetwork.com (Wayback, 27 March 2005)</ref> Each row had a date, title, short blurb, and author handle.

Published lists from that catalog are on [[Game Players Network decks]].

== After GPN ==

By November 2002 the committee had its own site at swccgpc.com. GPN still carried PC news into 2004. The PC later moved to starwarsccg.org (announced 10 June 2009).<ref name="domain2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102740/http://www.starwarsccg.org/news/news.php?id=69 New Domain and Server], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref> The Players Committee's community page later named GPN, with [[DeckTech]], among the sites its forums replaced as the main community hub.<ref name="pccn">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community-network/ Community Network], starwarsccg.org</ref>
